utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, before you start, I have to say something. This morning, we only have two hours in sitting. We will start now and we will have a break at 10.30. Then we will have 30 minutes' break. We will resume. We are advised to empty this room at 12.00 sharp. Another thing is that this Trial Chamber will issue an order about the scheduling arrangement before Christmas, because we are soon going to have the videolink witness and we have to share the courtroom with other cases. So there will be a lot of changes of our sitting schedule as well as the courtrooms. Yes, Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness QQ, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you at the outset of some of the problems we had yesterday, and please try to speak slowly and clearly, and also mindful of the time between your speaking and my speaking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand but I was always a fast speaker. However, I'll do my best. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While you were being held at the Heliodrom, sir, did you meet with a commander of one of the HV units that was located in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that, and can you just tell us the circumstances of how you came to meet with this individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met -- I saw Stela several times. He came to Heliodrom on more than one occasion. He took out those convicts, inmates. There were several HVO brigades, including Bruno Busic and some independent brigades. And as I said, I had known Stela for over 20 years. I didn't want to speak too much or even testify, but when he cursed me yesterday, he was trying to distribute all his forces, the police and all the rest of the units, but I must say that Stela and Tuta helped me personally a lot, but they harmed a lot of other people. And I came here to speak up for the dead. And if I may add to what I said yesterday, I can kill as well as Stela can kill. I can fight as well as Stela can fight. I was accused just as Stela. And I hate for anyone to be accused to be guilty. I find it difficult to testify against someone who is accused, but I wanted to help everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to cut you off. You have not answered my question. Please listen to my question and answer my question, please. The question that I put to you was: While you were at the Heliodrom, did you meet with a commander of any units of the army of Croatia, the HV army? Can you answer that question, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It was Ivan Kozul, the commander of the Tigers. He was commander at that time. There were many Bosnians at that time whom I knew. I knew Tigers from the Croatian war and Pumes and other units such as Thunderbolts, Gromovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall what the rank of this officer Kozul was and where was it you met him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single soldier, not a single officer at that time wore insignia or markings of rank. I can tell ranks, but when operations started, they took them off. I found out that the General was Bunik [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The General of what was Bunik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of that Tiger brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps you can assist us in this way: If you were familiar with the Tigers from Croatia and otherwise, what would the rank of their commanding officer -- what rank would their commanding officer or their senior officers possess? Would they be considered a general, a colonel, a major, or can you assist us, please, with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were promoted -- they went very fast up the ladder; major, colonel, general, brigade general. There were various ranks, and they were promoted very fast. It was not a Tito's officers' academy. It was wartime, and people went up the ladder very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before I move on, I just want to ask you; you do not recall the rank of this officer Kozul?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, he was a colonel and then he was promoted. I remember him when he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It may have been not General Bunik but Major-General. It needs to be clarified with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, we've had a request from translation for you to assist us further. When you mentioned a few minutes ago this other officer named Bunik, what title or rank did you give to him, because the translation was not clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Major-General, or Colonel-General. Commander of that regiment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The difference is between the words bojnik, which means "major," and Bunik, which may be a family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Around this time, did you see any other placements of HV units or equipment in the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them very well. All over the place, there was a lot of Croatian troops, various brigades deployed around the railway bridge towards Visnje, the cherry fields. That's one of the places where I worked pulling out the Croatian soldiers and prisoners. There were Tigers, Pumes, Thunderbolts, the Slavonian brigade, the 111th Brigade, the Rijeka unit. They were deployed in Rastani, Bijelo Polje, Mala Polje, and so on. There were some on Vakuf, at Varda. Heavy weaponry, tanks, Howitzers. I remember Varda because that's where Blaz Kraljevic was, and I remember the road because I did some digging by that road. We were digging trenches, and I remember that road well because that's the road we took from Ljubuski to Heliodrom --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Witness, I'm going to cut you off, please. Did you, in fact, as you were just saying -- you've given us in the last couple minutes a couple of locations. Were you required to work in those number of locations, and is that one of the reasons why you have the information that you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A lot of prisoners were taken to work on numerous locations, wherever there was a line between the BH army and the HVO. And they went in groups to various locations. I was in all of those places while I was imprisoned in the camp, and I was a detainee for nine, ten months.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to direct your attention to one particular location, and I'm going to mention to you -- you may have been at this location more than once. At the moment, I'm asking you about the first time you were there. And that is at the location called Brkanovo Brdo. Did you ever work at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Brkanovo Brdo, or Brkan Hill, was a place I worked about a month, together with another 10 or 15 workers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness, before you continue with that story, let me ask you, in connection with working at this location or coming back from that location to the Heliodrom, did you have any encounters with any HVO soldiers that you had had dealings with or had contact with before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I met up there with a certain Robi who had beaten us in Duvno, where he was drunk a lot of the time. I remember him well because he's the one who broke two of my ribs. And when we were coming back from Brkanovo Brdo, a small van was picking up the camp inmates, and there was a waste dump nearby. The van was picking up inmates along the way. He picked us up near this waste dump. The van stopped. The soldier who was guarding us was also tipsy, but he was a nice man otherwise. I don't remember clearly, but I kept a diary on critical days at least. He took us out and lined us up, and he selected those people whom he knew, I think. He took them away from the bus, from the van, about ten metres or so, and I heard a shot, maybe even a burst of gunfire, a full clip perhaps. Those men did not return to the van. We were panic-stricken. We thought that our turn would come too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Witness, I'm going to stop you there for a moment ask you a few questions about that. You said, for instance, "He took them away from the bus, from the van." Who is the "he" you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. You've already warned me about this. I meant Robi. I had him in mind all the time; Robert, Robi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And how many men did he identify and take away, as you told us about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I want to continue on. Was there another time that you were working at the Brkanovo Brdo in which you could again see things happening in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I worked there on several occasions. One of the dugouts was destroyed. The retranslating device of Mostar is located there, used to help land planes. I don't know who destroyed it. Maybe the Serbian army from Velez, maybe the BH army. Perhaps the BH army couldn't do it from this low point. But it doesn't matter anyway. On two or three occasions, shelling of the old bridge, Stari Most, was announced, and I remember well - I have a good memory - there were many troops there, and officers forced us to go on a hill, and I heard somebody saying on a Motorola that all barrels should be pointed at Stari Most and that shelling should begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Witness, I'm going to stop you there for a moment. I'd like, with the usher's assistance, to show you a couple of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: First off, could I ask, please, that the witness be shown, out of Exhibit P11, it's photo number 16 specifically.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. That will not identify the witness, so I suggest this could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I don't think it will be disputed at this point, I hope, that this is a photograph of Mount Hum. Can you see any features, man-made features, on that mountain that you can identify as having been constructed in connection with the war? And perhaps you yourself may have been involved in working at some of those locations. Maybe -- if you can take -- orient yourself, please, and perhaps take a pointer, and if you can point out any of the features on the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for giving me this opportunity to object. I have tried to keep my silence so far, although the witness is not answering the questions. He is just saying whatever he pleases. But the Prosecutor has a lot of experience, and he is trying to lead him. We have no problem with this photograph. We don't challenge it, but at least the Prosecutor could have asked him what he recognised on this photograph. However, we let this pass. I think there is a problem with the way the witness is being examined. I think the question should have been, Please, what you see on the photograph, instead of saying to him what it was and asking him to confirm. The Prosecutor has just said what this photograph was all about. And all he left for the witness to do was to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage in these proceedings, is there a bona fide dispute that this feature is Mount Hum? I will be surprised and shocked if that's the case. Why are we wasting time in this sort of manner?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Since there is an objection, Mr. Scott, you may lead the witness step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you point outside to us, sir, any of the man-made features on this geographic feature that you are familiar with, just by points of reference? I don't mean every one of them, but if you're familiar with or were involved in working in connection with any of them, can you please point them out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it very well. And I am responding to Defence counsel; I don't even need this picture to tell you. I've worked this on several locations. There's an old dugout left over from the Turkish times, PATs, Pams, and the recoilless cannon were located, stationed there, and we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. It would help us, as I've asked you to do, can you take the pointer, please, and point out on this photograph the location you're presently telling us about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, well, that was awfully quick. You were just telling us about a particular bunker. Can you point that out, please, with your pointer and stay on it for a moment so everyone can see what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you work at any of the other locations, any other man-made features on that photograph that you can see, in connection with forced labour? And if you can, just point them out briefly to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not marking those because it's not that central, but I wanted the Chamber to have some orientation to the overall location for purposes of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, sir, that, at least in part, you could see on this photograph the location near -- forgive me -- Brkanovo Brdo, or at least close to it. Can you point out on the photograph as close as you can - and I acknowledge it may be off the page - but as close as you can where that feature or location is located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the right-hand side, it's on the right-hand side of Brkanovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There's a bit more photograph that could be displayed -- well, for some reason, it doesn't seem to be on that version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, can we back away from the photo a bit. My apologies, Mr. President. The version on this is a bit different. It's the same photo, but it has been cut a bit differently. Can I ask the usher's assistance, please, to put this map, number 16, on the ELMO, please. Now, if you can pull out so you can see the far right part of the picture, please. A bit more. Perhaps move the whole picture a little bit to the left -- we don't need to see the other part now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, can you now--

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, you just cut off more of it. What I want to see is the far right of the picture, please. I guess that's the best we can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, my apologies for the difficulties. Can you please now point on that photograph, as close as you can, the feature Brkanovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's right here that this small depression starts, Brkanovo Brdo. And here to the right is the link with Hum. There is a road which leads to Siroki Brijeg, down to Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned, I believe, a few minutes ago in your testimony, that from this location where you were working, you could see the old bridge known as Stari Most. In fact, that's what that means in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, very well indeed, both from Hum and Brkanovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Could I ask the witness next to be shown, please, from the same photograph 11, photo number 3. And Madam Registrar, if I could have your assistance on this, perhaps you could -- if you have a yellow sticky or something, you could block any identifying marks on the photograph. Mr. Usher could you put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Witness QQ, can you please identify what you see in that photograph. And there again, perhaps it can be shown more -- a little bit more on the right side of the photograph. Can you tell us, please, what feature you see prominent in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall turn my head so that the lord doesn't object. I have never -- I have never been on the old bridge. And I'll tell you now, there was some scaffolding here, and there was a rope and some old tyres hanging on a concrete pillar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness, all right, I understand what you've told us just now, and you say you've never physically walked or been on the bridge. My question to you is this the sort of view -- is this what you could see, something like this, when you said you were at this Brkanovo Brdo location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, of course, I was not next to the old bridge, around the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I'm sorry if my question wasn't clear. Let me go back. You were working at this location you told us about a few minutes ago, at Brkanovo Brdo. You told us that, from that location, you could see the Stari Most.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, does this photograph represent what you could see, approximately? I'm not saying exactly this, but this is approximately what you could see from that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that you heard -- overheard an order being given that all guns come to bear on the bridge. Can you tell us more about that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. We were still working, getting ready, bringing the shells in their crates, ammunition. There was quite a lot of it, and naturally, officers and soldiers and those serving howitzers and tanks, and I could hear Motorolas when orders were issued to turn all the barrels on the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From where you were -- excuse me, from where you were located, could you see any particular -- excuse me, artillery tanks or equipment that appeared to be firing in the direction of the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of us took shelter behind a node. We tried to get some shelter. And as far as I can remember, there were three tanks, three howitzers, a number of rocket launchers, then anti-aircraft guns and machine-guns, the self-propelled recoilless guns, and so on. I'm familiar with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you specifically concerning the tanks that you saw, can you identify those tanks as being part of or associated with any particular military unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes. I knew. I remember that there were one or two tanks which came from the Croatian army, and they had no plates, no registration. It was covered with a plastic sticker over the -- over the paint where it said -- where it should say "Tigrovi," the Tigers. There were also HVO, and they did say -- they did have inscriptions "HVO" so that one could clearly see that. And all the Mostarans who were in the camp can confirm it. They know better than I do various places. I know only the places that I remembered because it was -- because these were the places where I suffered. I also remember places where I felt well. So that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question about the marking on this particular tank. You've told us that these markings -- or some of the markings on the tank were covered over. I want to give you the opportunity to explain this. If markings were covered over, how could you identify the tank as an HV tank or a Tigers tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew many members of the Tigers, and that was how I could prove, see, spot, know, because they were naturally Croatian soldiers, and they were handling their own weapons, and the HVO had their weapons, and they used those.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to tell the Chamber, please, of what you could observe on that day, at that time, could you see any officer -- did you see any HV or HVO officers around the location where these tanks were firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where Stela and Tuta turned up, and Reuf Ajanovic, a fiend, the man who married Mirjana Barbaric, and she was a cook up there, a good woman, and I knew that Ajanovic from before, from Iraq where we worked there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, how far away were you from this group of officers that you saw on the hillside?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we again have some problems with translation. I know we talked yesterday with our distinguished interpreters how difficult it is - and we all understand that - how very difficult it is to interpret this gentleman, this witness, because even for us it is very difficult to follow him, even though we speak the same language. He said -- he answered the Prosecutor's question if he had seen some Croatian officers, and that is line 18, he used the word "happened to be there, turned up there." It means they just happened to be there. They turned up there. They found themselves there. So it is an idiom in Bosnian-Croatian version of the language. It does not mean that they were there all the time. They just happened to be there. They turned up there. They fetched up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a problem of the language. I believe that the interpreters have done their utmost to translate for us. They are very, very careful in those things. I do not know the situation in the former Yugoslavia, but in China, there are thousands and thousands of dialects. It's difficult to understand certain dialects. At this point, first, I would like to ask the witness to speak very slowly and clearly so that we could get all what you are going to say. And secondly, Mr. Scott, would you please clear up that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: First off, Witness, let's go back to the names that you mentioned just now because I think counsel is correct that they may not have been --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- fully indicated on the transcript. So the officers that you saw that day, at the time you've been telling us about when you saw the Stari Most and the tanks firing, who did you see on the hillside, and if you can, give us the names very slowly and if you can assist us with even a spelling, that would be of help as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Vinko Martinovic, called Stela. There was Tuta. There was this Kozul. And there were a number of commanders whose names I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm looking at the transcript, Mr. President. That seems to be correct. In terms of the question of counsel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The witness said, after Kozul, "And a number of senior officers whose names I do not know." The witness said very clearly that, "It was a large number of senior officers whose names I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the objection is, Your Honour. If that's what the witness said, that's what the witness said. I do think it's fair to say that, in the prior answer, I think I recall him saying the name "Ajanovic." If that's the question that counsel is suggesting he didn't mention one of the names again, I would suggest that I did hear the name "Ajanovic" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies to my learned friend. It is very clearly, again, the translation is not as it should be, and the witness has verified. We all hear that, and there can be no dispute, Colleague Scott. When the witness listed names, he said, "Vinko Martinovic, Tuta [sic]; Vinko Martinovic, Stela; Kozul; and a large number of senior commanders whose names I do not know," and that is not how the transcript says. And I think it is very clear, and the witness confirms -- I mean, he confirms with his head that he said that so I do not see what the dispute is. I merely wanted to intervene because of the Honourable Court, because I wanted the transcript to reflect properly what the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Krsnik, if there were a race there to see who spoke faster, you would win.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, on page 13, line 21 and 22, there's a reference to a - I'm sorry, I keep looking up and losing it - Reuf and another name. And all I simply asked, because of the question that was raised about accuracy, I asked the witness to go back and also give us correctly that name. That's the only point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not the names that are at stake here. It seems that there's a complete misunderstanding here. It has nothing to do with the names. We are only talking about accurate interpretation. We want the accurate interpretation of what the witness says, nothing else, and that is why I stood up. I'm not interested in any names at all. But when the witness said the number, that is, "a large number of senior commanders," "of senior commanders whose names I don't know," is what's at dispute here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have been informed that the witness said that those people happened to be there, or turned out to be, or something like this. You may ask some questions along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Thank you. Mr. President, it may not be important to the counsel, but it is important, I submit, to the record that the names be correct, and that's why, again, I asked the witness to confirm and to give us the correct spelling if he had also previously mentioned the name, which I believe he did, Reuf Ajanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we go further, did you tell us a few minutes ago that you also saw someone named Reuf, R-E-U-F, Ajanovic at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I remember it very well. A big man like Stela, strongly built, and I know him. I recognised him up there at Siroki Brijeg and in Mostar, and on the front lines. Reuf Ajanovic. He used to work for Hidrogradnja and we worked together at a construction site in Iraq.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... on that point. Witness QQ, perhaps you have heard some of the exchanges over the last few minutes. Counsel has raised a question over the proper interpretation, I suppose, of what you just said. Did you see a number of officers who -- and I cannot say this in any way in your language, of course, but something to the effect that these officers showed up there or were seen to turn up at this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These people were there. Now, how they fetched up there, how they happened to be there, I do not know. I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that's all the clarification I can give the Chamber. There was never a suggestion, I don't believe, either by the witness or by me, that those officers -- any particular one of those officers gave any particular order. All the witness has said is that he saw this grouping of officers -- a number of officers at that location. How they turned up there or not, he hasn't given us any more detail. And I think that's all I'm asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness QQ, we're changing subjects again, and I say that because -- just to avoid confusion. Did you ever have a conversation while being held at the Heliodrom with one of the senior officials there about somehow obtaining your release?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked that Boro and Smiljanic and a number of people, and I said one fights to survive and then realises that his life is nothing but a fly's life. So I asked who is the number one in the camp? Can I go to him and see him? I didn't know the man, and I cannot guarantee whether that man was or was not. But he went to ask him to admit me, to see me, and it's somebody called -- it's one Praljak. That is what I was told, that he was a general, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, excuse me. You just said that you cannot guarantee whether that man was or was not. Now what did you mean by that? Whether he was or was not the head of the Heliodrom, or what were you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I cannot guarantee, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with this man named Praljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had it. Yes, I could even identify him, unless the man has changed seriously. Can I go out to third countries? Because I have been abroad, I have been in France. Can you let me go in some way or other? I could not suffer the treatment any longer. I had lost a lot of weight. I was weakened. And he said, I'm not for that, for the exchange, for release because there is Jadranko Prlic for that. And once again, I then met Jadranko Prlic at the Ero Hotel [Realtime transcript read in error "^ Hotel"] when we were assigned there to dig and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You just mentioned the name of a hotel, I believe. What location is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Hotel Ero. That is what I heard, that the hotel was called Ero. That's where they held their meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go into private session for one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness QQ, we are on the subject of possibility of prisoners at the Heliodrom obtaining their release from custody as a result of money being paid. Did you ever have any conversations with this Reuf Ajanovic about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I talked to him at Siroki Brijeg. I learned that Reuf, whom I knew, had changed his name to Stipo Barbaric and married a woman by the name of Mirjana Barbaric from Siroki Brijeg. I did talk to him, but without any result. Nothing was achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Mr. Ajanovic took you to meet somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. On the 13th of October, he took me to Siroki Brijeg to see Tuta in a black Mercedes. I didn't recognise him at first, but I did later on, as we talked. I also met Mr. Stela there, and Tuta, in a coffee bar. I was standing aside like an orphan. Mr. Tuta even treated me to a drink and some food.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there for a moment before you proceed with your story. One clarification. You said just now that, "I didn't recognise him at first, but I did later on as we talked." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reuf, I meant that his name was Reuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, could I please ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 704.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I'm not mistaken, I believe it's that notorious list of members, so I would make the same objection that Mr. Scott made to me. How is this relevant when it refers to the month of November? I'm talking about that list, you remember, which we discussed yesterday or the day before yesterday. So what is the relevance of this document now in relation to this witness and the month that he is talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, you may give us some explanations about relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Your Honour, it could be that if the witness sees the name and identifies a name and can associate it with a person he's talking about, and he can confirm to us that he saw this same person closely associated with Tuta in October of 1993, which is only a short time before this document was prepared, because it refers to the salary list for November, so we are only talking a difference of a couple of weeks, I think it's appropriate and this Chamber can then draw whatever inferences it chooses in terms of Mr. Ajanovic was a member in November and, according to this witness, a logical inference that the Chamber can draw is that he was also a member a few weeks earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed. But the conclusion will be arrived at by the Judges themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Scott, and with the President's permission, I don't know if I made a mistake or the interpretation made a mistake. I was quite surprised when the witness said that he was taken to see, I thought he said Mr. Tudjman in a Mercedes. Was it Mr. Tuta or Mr. Tudjman? Because I wrote down Tudjman and I noticed that the interpreter has Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think I know the answer, Your Honour, but I'll ask the witness, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, just a moment ago, when you testified to being taken to Siroki Brijeg to meet with someone, who did you meet with there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A couple of questions, Mr. President, but I'll start with that one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man who called himself Stipo Barbaric after changing his name, he came several times. He was in the Convicts Battalion a long time with Tuta, and he took prisoners from Heliodrom away. He took me out. I didn't know where he was taking me. He just called out my name when I was in a room in Heliodrom. He took me out, put me in a Mercedes, and took me to Siroki Brijeg to Tuta, the commander. All the information is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much; my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, on Exhibit 704 and in the Serbo-Croatian version, the original language version --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Usher, I think you may help us do this more efficiently. If I can direct you to -- using the references, Mr. Usher, if you could find the page in the B/C/S version that has the stamp numbers 00795363, in the last four digits being 5363, and show that to the witness, that would assist. And Mr. President, Your Honours, in the English version, if you choose to follow in that, it would be on what's marked page 11, which I'll qualify in one moment, but it would be on page 11. Now, what's happened apparently, Your Honour, at some point, is the pages have been rearranged, and I apologise for that, but -- so it won't be -- page 10 may not literally be the tenth sheet in the bundle of documents, but if you find numbered page 10 in the lower, right column -- and actually, I should say page 11 - my mistake - page 11, numbered 11, it corresponds to that document, and I apologise for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Witness QQ, on that page, which I'll refer to as 5363, can you cast your eyes down that list of names, please. I don't want you to take a great deal of time to do this, but can you see on this list the name of this person that you've been telling us about in the last few minutes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can identify a lot of names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me focus your attention, please, for now. This man that you've been telling us about, Mr. Ajanovic, do you see his name on this list? And if so, can you indicate by number, perhaps, what number that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not here. It's not here on this page, either Barbaric or Ajanovic. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I don't want to belabour this. I just want to, with the usher's assistance, make sure we're on the same page. It's 5363. Very well. Mr. President, because of the time constraints and otherwise, I won't pursue it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that this man took you to Siroki Brijeg. Tell us what happened after you got to Siroki Brijeg, in this regard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I found it. It's a photocopy. 44. Captain, it says. Number 44, I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does both the first and last name indicated on this list correspond to the man you knew by this name, the same man who took you to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. And I'm sure, 1.000 percent, not 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, could we put it on the ELMO so that we can see what number 44 is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Witness. Thank you for that. Can you go forward, please, and listen to my question. After you were taken to meet Tuta in Siroki Brijeg, what happened? What did you talk about? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tuta recognised me, and I take my hat off to him. I can thank this man for being alive today. He bought me a beer and some food, and he told this Barbaric to take me to the hotel and put me in a room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber, please, if you know, by indicating how it was, as far as you know, that Mr. -- the situation by which Mr. Tuta would have recognised you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know each other from Croatia. I also know Tuta from Stuttgart. I know him through Croatian battlefields when I was leaving Croatia. The HOS and the Croatian army was on my back, and I had to leave. I couldn't join. I wanted to join the Croatian army because my first circle was in -- sorry, the first bread I earned was in Croatia. I wanted this certificate, which I mentioned yesterday. I went to Bosnia first, then to France to some friends, and then I went back to Bosnia where I was arrested. I don't know how it all came about. Anyway, I came to Tuta to report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, my apologies. I'm just trying to adjust the outline according to what the witness is telling us, so if I could have just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You said something, I think a few moments ago, that as a result of this exchange with Tuta, you were then placed in a hotel in Siroki Brijeg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was the Park Hotel, which was more than half of which was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did you remain at that location, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent over 100 days there, 120-something days. We were carrying out works, going to all kinds of places. There were several convicts. And when we were investigating, this prisoner who was together with me, and I, we were released together. But I will tell you more about it as you continue to question me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Just now, the person you said, the prisoner who was with you, this is the man you identified earlier in private session. Is that correct, without saying his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, during this time, were you required to perform any sort of labour or work on projects or properties in the area surrounding Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I worked everywhere. I'm sorry I have to say this. I was at Tuta's villa. You gave me a picture, and I recognised it among five pictures. There was a swimming pool and a villa. We did repair jobs. They took us to all kinds of places. Tuta didn't know about this. They later -- he later reprimanded those people for taking us there. They were crude and drunken. I didn't want to say too much because, at one point, I had lost control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How many days, approximately, did you work at this location that -- I want to use your words. The place you described just now as Tuta's villa; how many days or times did you work at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about ten days; I'm not sure. After so many years, you could forget your own child's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lost a lot of family.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher, please, to provide the witness with Exhibits 25.3, 25.5, and 25.6, which could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry that I'm on my feet so often yesterday [as interpreted], but it's for the sake of the record. I have the feeling -- and the same thing often happens in our courtrooms and in our system, when something does not come into the record, we have to intervene. A large portion of what the witness has said is missing. It wasn't translated at all. In line 22 -- perhaps I should explain. This witness is using a lot of words which you might call slang in English, and we in Croatia would say that these are terms used in slang all over Bosnia and all Bosnians understand them. But I understand it's a very difficult job for interpreters, especially if they are not originally from Bosnia. The language of this witness is full of such terms. So if the Prosecutor could ask the witness to speak more slowly and stick to standard language, because I see that there is a lot of misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? I apologise. That's the language I know from Croatia, and I know a lot of languages. I took those terms over from Croatia. These are the terms that I'm used to. That's how I was born and what I was brought up with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I'll ask the witness to speak more slowly. I'm not going to attempt to tell him which words to use, what dialect or -- if someone wants to use that terminology which was used a few minutes ago, I'm not going to ask him to modify his normal language that he speaks in. But I will ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, please, please speak slowly and articulate your words as best you can, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Mr. Krsnik, your objection is correctly recorded in the transcript. I believe that the interpreters will check it during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wasn't exactly clear. Just so I have some idea, although I guess in some sense it doesn't matter, but we are going to sit until when?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness QQ, if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could put 25.3 on the ELMO first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, please listen very specifically to my questions. I'm not going to engage you in any lengthy discussion about these photographs, but if you look, first of all, at 25.3, do you recognise anything that's shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The swimming pool, the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what are those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my mind, it's the villa. That's what it was called. A large house -- a larger-than-usual house in Bosnia is called a villa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is this the same house that you were telling us about a few moments ago, where you were taken to perform labour on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't know to whom it belonged. I found out later while I was working, landscaping, so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you look next at 25.5, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same thing. What am I to look at? It's the same thing from a different side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally, 25.6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing all over again. I can hardly make a mistake about it. I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, I'm editing. I'm looking at my notes and editing down, omitting a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness QQ, can you tell us, please - only to direct your attention - was there a time when you sought a new pair of shoes? If you can remember anything about that, tell us about that situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't seek a new pair of shoes. It's towards the end, Mr. Prosecutor. That part is towards the end, about shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you what -- where it is, in what order. Did there come a time when you were provided or wanted to obtain a new pair of shoes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got everything new, a whole new set, from Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was towards my release. I got a change of clothes. I fared much better than anyone else. I had everything. But that was towards the end, before I got out. I got a whole new set of clothes. And I wouldn't like to say anything against Tuta, and I believe I haven't. I wish him luck and good health.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me come back --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You seem to want to talk about that later, and I will ask you questions, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you hear me? My microphone seems to be on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before, then, we come to that, Witness QQ, can you tell the Chamber, please, did you ever see any senior officials from the Republic of Croatia come to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw -- I know Andabak very well, and I saw Gojko Susak. He wore a leather jacket. He is dead now. One shouldn't speak badly of dead people. And a lot of other people. They were going around on inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How many times -- can you tell the Chamber, please, how many times did you see Gojko Susak in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice. Twice, that I remember. But we were concealed a lot of the time, so I saw them on two or three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Susak touring the Siroki Brijeg area with anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Tuta would be one of those, a number of officials. He came specifically to ask a prisoner, Rudi, to leave because he used to be a pilot in the JNA, so that that Rudi left with him or somebody else. I don't know. I never saw him again. And later on, I learned that that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Rudi left with who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that he left with Susak. He wasn't in the camp any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, did there come a time, again, when the topic of your being released came up in discussions in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I sent a letter through the Red Cross, and you know what a letter looks like, a certificate to a friend of mine in France who was with Ante Roso. I forget to mention that Ante Roso was there, too. And he interceded on my behalf. I wrote to him where I was being kept, and he interceded, so that I spent a month with him after I came out of the camp. He interceded with Tudjman and Susak to keep me alive, not to have me killed and to let me go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go to private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as we had agreed, I should start the cross-examination of this witness, but right at the very beginning, I have a big sets of questions, they all concern one and the same matter, we should have to go into private session and then we will have to have a break. So I think we shall be happy to accept your suggestion and leave it for Monday morning. And meanwhile, I'm sorry to take over your role, far be it from me, but really this witness should not be communicating with anyone until we undertake our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this is what I'm going to say. Witness, I have to give you a piece of advice, as I did with all other witnesses before this Tribunal. Please do not speak to anybody about your evidence until your testimony has been completed, and also do not let anybody speak to you about it. Mr. Scott, this Trial Chamber would grant you leave to take a statement on the alleged threat the witness claimed before he came here to give evidence, with the presence of the representative from the Registrar. Your interview with this witness should only be limited to this very issue, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Having said that, we will adjourn until Monday morning, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 11.56 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
